react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary enrichment paradigms — RaMP multi-database ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and mummichog m/z-network analysis — converge on a single biological domain as the overwhelming winner: the arachidonic acid / eicosanoid metabolic network. In the RaMP ORA the top-ranked pathway is WikiPathways WP:WP167 "Eicosanoid synthesis" (FDR = 2.1 × 10⁻¹³, fold-enrichment 1251, five driver metabolites: arachidonic acid, leukotriene A₄, 15-deoxy-Δ¹²·¹⁴-prostaglandin J₂, 5-HETE, and 15-HETE). The same five compounds map to multiple SMPDB drug-action pathways (rofecoxib, acetylsalicylic acid, etoricoxib, etc.) because NSAIDs share the arachidonic acid substrate as their mechanistic anchor. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently ranks KEGG:hsa00590 "Arachidonic acid metabolism" as rank-1 (p_raw = 0.0396), with four of the same driver metabolites (arachidonic acid, leukotriene A₄, 15-HETE, 5-HETE) contributing to the enrichment. Mummichog, which exploits empirical mass-network topology, places "Arachidonic acid metabolism" as its top pathway (p = 0.0059) with 11 matched metabolites including 15-deoxy-PGJ₂, prostaglandin intermediates, and HPETE precursors — confirming that the LOX (5-HETE/15-HETE) and COX (PGJ₂) branches of the same network are co-activated. A secondary KEGG hit (hsa00920, sulfur metabolism, p = 0.0396) reflects the thiosulfate metabolite. The three non-lipid inputs — methylmalonic acid, 5-androstenediol, and xanthine — do not pass FDR in any ORA method, suggesting they are peripheral to the core perturbation. The biological story is one of cyclooxygenase / lipoxygenase pathway activation: arachidonic acid is mobilised, shunted through both the COX branch (producing the J₂ prostaglandin) and the 5-LOX/15-LOX branches (producing LTA₄, 5-HETE, and 15-HETE), consistent with an inflammatory, prostanoid, or electrophilic lipid signalling response in the treatment condition. The InChIKey reconciliation confirmed all nine input metabolites are structurally distinct entities with no namespace conflicts, ensuring that each compound represents a genuine biological signal rather than a database aliasing artefact.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary enrichment paradigms converge on Arachidonic acid metabolism as the dominant perturbed pathway. RaMP-DB ORA (merged multi-DB) ranks Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) first among all Reactome, SMPDB, KEGG and WikiPathways entries with FDR = 2.12e-13 and p_raw = 1.18e-15; five lipid mediators drive this hit: arachidonic acid (C00219), leukotriene A4 (C00909), 5-HETE (C04805), 15-HETE (C04742) and 15-deoxy-delta12,14-PGJ2 (C14717). MetaboAnalystR PSEA (KEGG) independently confirms KEGG:hsa00590 (Arachidonic acid metabolism) as the top pathway with p = 2.49e-06, driven by the same four arachidonate-derived compounds. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis independently ranks Arachidonic acid metabolism (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism) at the top of its network-ranked list (p = 0.0058), with six of the input lipid mediators found in the empirical-compound network. The cross-paradigm winner spans five metabolites that are all confirmed members of the KEGG:hsa00590 pathway by direct hit evidence. Thiosulfate (C05529), methylmalonic acid (C02170), 5-androstenediol (C04295) and xanthine (C00385) are absent from the top pathways of all three methods, suggesting they are peripherally altered or biologically secondary to the core lipid-mediator perturbation.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary enrichment paradigms converge on Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) as the overwhelming winner. RaMP-DB ORA assigns this pathway FDR = 2.12e-13 (fold enrichment 1250.9, p_raw = 1.18e-15), ranking it first among all Reactome, SMPDB, KEGG, and WikiPathways entries. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis independently ranks Arachidonic acid metabolism as its top hit (p = 0.0045). Five input metabolites — arachidonic acid (KEGG:C00219), leukotriene A4 (KEGG:C00909), 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2 (KEGG:C14717), 5-HETE (KEGG:C04805), and 15-HETE (KEGG:C04742) — are confirmed members of WP:WP167. RaMP additionally identifies Rofecoxib Action Pathway (SMPDB:SMP00087), Salicylate-sodium Action Pathway (SMPDB:SMP00708), and Acetylsalicylic Acid Action Pathway (SMPDB:SMP00083) as co-enriched at identical FDR = 5.54e-13, each sharing the same five driver metabolites. The remaining four inputs — thiosulfate (KEGG:C05529), methylmalonic acid (KEGG:C02170), 5-androstenediol (KEGG:C04295), and xanthine (KEGG:C00385) — do not appear in the top-10 hits of any paradigm, indicating they are peripheral to the core lipid-mediator perturbation.
